Course pack

MS-DOS 4.00 and FreeBSD 15.1, from the boot sector to the shell

By Francesco Valerio Buccoli (francesco@buccoli.com).

MS-DOS 2d04cacFreeBSD release/15.1.0about 5 min read
Francesco Valerio Buccoli · francesco@buccoli.com

A university Operating Systems course built on two real, complete source trees: MS-DOS 4.00, released as open source by Microsoft and IBM in 2024, and FreeBSD 15.1. Each module follows one part of a PC operating system, the boot code, the kernel and the shell, through both systems, with every claim tied to a line of source code at a fixed commit.

Modules#

Module Topic MS-DOS 4.00 FreeBSD 15.1
0. The lab Building MS-DOS from source, booting it, the FreeBSD machine v4.0/src build tree Installation, /usr/src
1. Booting From the BIOS to the first user program FDBOOT, MSBOOT, MSLOAD, SYSINIT, CONFIG.SYS mbr, boot0, boot1/boot2, gptboot, BTX, loader, locore, mi_startup, SYSINIT()
2. The kernel System calls, files, memory and programs INT 21h, SFT/JFT, FAT.ASM, MCB arena, EXEC, device drivers syscall, file descriptors, msdosfs, vm_map, fork/execve, cdevsw
3. The shell COMMAND.COM and /bin/sh Resident/transient design, batch files, pipes through temporary files Parser and evaluator, real pipes, job control
4. Assembly Machine code and assembly language 8086 real mode, MASM 5.10, DEBUG, INT 21h x86-64, NASM and AT&T syntax, syscall, libsys stubs
5. The toolchain From C to a running program Microsoft C 5.10, OMF, LINK, MZ .EXE vs .COM, memory models, LIB clang, ELF, ld, crt1.o, shared libraries, rtld
6. Hardware BIOS, ports, interrupts, drivers and consoles BIOS services, port I/O, the device driver chain, CON, CLOCK$, ANSI.SYS newbus, interrupts, the vt console, termios, timecounters
7. File systems Disks and file systems FAT12/16, the DPB, CHKDSK UFS2, inodes, soft updates, msdosfs
8. Memory and configuration Memory and configuration in practice Conventional, upper, expanded and extended memory, CONFIG.SYS, EMM386 Virtual memory, vmstat, rc.conf, rc.d, sysctl, loader.conf
9. Toolsmith The same tools on both systems Tools in assembly, C and .BAT Tools in assembly, C and sh

Modules 0-3 follow one part of the system through both source trees; Modules 4-9 are hands-on: in every lab students build or run something on the real MS-DOS 4.00 and on a real FreeBSD 15.1 machine, and every output shown in the notes was captured that way. Each module has lecture notes with block diagrams, deep study cases with source listings from both systems, labs and homework. Lab starter files are in labs/, and a slide deck per module is in slides/. The HTML edition (dist/students/index.html) needs no software: open it in a browser, also offline.

Instructor edition#

Model answers to every lab question and exercise, grading rubrics, teaching notes and the reference solutions of all lab programs form a separate instructor edition (instructor/ and dist/instructor/). It is not public, so that students cannot find the answers. Teachers who use the course can ask the author for it.

Getting started#

Module 0 sets up the lab: it fetches the pinned sources, builds MS-DOS 4.00 from source in DOSBox-X, makes a bootable floppy image, and creates the FreeBSD 15.1 virtual machine (Hyper-V, from the official image) that the FreeBSD labs use. The course was developed and every output captured on Windows 11 with Hyper-V; other hosts and hypervisors should work but have not been tested.

How the course cites code#

Project Pinned at Licence
MS-DOS 4.00 (github.com/microsoft/MS-DOS, folder v4.0) commit 2d04cacc5322951f187bb17e017c12920ac8ebe2 MIT
FreeBSD 15.1 (github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src) tag release/15.1.0, commit 96841ea08dcfa84b954a32dc5ae1a26c28966cf4 BSD (mostly 2-clause)

Every source listing links to its exact lines at those commits and is checked mechanically against them (python tools/check_citations.py). The sources themselves are not stored in this repository: tools/fetch_sources.ps1 fetches them. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

Repository layout#

Path Contents
course/ Student-facing notes, one Markdown file per module
labs/ Lab starter files and test data (DOS files keep CRLF line endings)
instructor/ Instructor edition only: model answers, rubrics, teaching notes and reference solutions in instructor/code/
diagrams/ Block diagrams: JSON specs and the SVG files generated from them
slides/ Slide outlines (*.outline.json) and generated decks (*.pptx)
tools/ Source fetcher, citation checker, MS-DOS build and run tools, FreeBSD VM tools, HTML, diagram and slide builders
dist/ Generated HTML: dist/students/ (and dist/instructor/ in the instructor edition)
src-ext/ The fetched third-party sources (not committed)
build/ Build outputs: the MS-DOS build tree, disk images, the FreeBSD VM disk, rendered PNGs (not committed)

Tools#

Command What it does
tools/fetch_sources.ps1 Fetch both source trees at the pinned commits
python tools/check_citations.py Check every citation and listing in the course against the sources
python tools/build_dos.py Build MS-DOS 4.00 from source in DOSBox-X (about 2 minutes)
python tools/make_floppy.py Make a bootable 1.44 MB floppy image from the build
python tools/dos_run.py ["CMD" ...] Boot the image interactively, or run commands on MS-DOS 4.00 and print their output (--file adds files to the disk, --conf-extra changes the emulated PC, for example its CPU type or memory size, --keep saves the disk)
python tools/dos_tools.py --dir DIR "CMD" ... Run the 1988 Microsoft toolchain from the source tree (MASM 5.10, C 5.10, LINK, LIB, EXE2BIN) on a folder of your computer
tools/screen.asm SCREEN.COM: copies the text screen to the output (captures messages printed before AUTOEXEC.BAT)
tools/boot_snapshot.ps1 Boot any disk image in DOSBox-X and save a picture of the screen (boot-sector homework)
tools/new_bsd_vm.ps1 Create the FreeBSD 15.1 Hyper-V virtual machine from the official disk image
python tools/bsd_run.py ["CMD" ...] Run commands in the FreeBSD VM over SSH and print their output (--put/--get copy files, --shell opens a session)
tools/hyperv_console.ps1, tools/hyperv_type.ps1 Type at the FreeBSD VM's console and take screenshots of it (before SSH works)
python tools/diagrams.py [--png] Generate the block diagrams in diagrams/ from their JSON specs (--png also renders slide images)
python tools/build_html.py Build the self-contained HTML edition in dist/
python tools/build_slides.py [--render] Build the slide decks from slides/*.outline.json (verifying every code slide); --render exports PNGs through PowerPoint
